title: §.XI open: Close Variata defense with Chemnitz judgment — Lyser 1594, Bajer 1676, Hannekenius Declarat. cite the same Chemnitz words
pass_a_gloss: §. XI. Our disputation instituted for the Variata Confession not to be attacked or rejected, we close with the judgment of D. Martin Chemnitz a little earlier alleged, On the Controversies which in the prior time were moved and agitated about certain Articles of the Augsburg Confession, and edited both by D. Polycarp Leyser in the year 1594 at Wittenberg and by D. Bajer in the year 1676 at Jena, praised also by both, and indeed most recently planed smooth in the saying of the Wittenberg theologian D. Hannekenius, Theological Declaration on the true Estimation of the Augsburg Confession, Preliminary Question 4, toward the end, page 6, whose Chemnitzian judgment's words run thus:
pass_b_english: §. XI. We close this defense of the Variata — that it is not to be attacked or thrown out — with the Chemnitz judgment already cited a little above.
It is the piece On the Controversies once stirred about certain Augsburg Confession articles, edited by Polycarp Leyser at Wittenberg in 1594 and again by Bajer at Jena in 1676, praised by both.

Most recently the Wittenberg theologian Hannekenius smoothed the same saying in his Theological Declaration on the true Estimation of the Augsburg Confession (Preliminary Question 4, near the end, p. 6).
source_text:
§. XI.
Disputationem nostram pro Confessione Variata non impugnanda aut rejicienda institutam, claudimus paulò ante allegato judicio D. MARTINI CHEMNITII de Controversiis quae superiori tempore, circa quosdam August. Confess. Articulos, motae & agitatae sunt, & tam à D. Polycarpo Lysero Anno 1594. Wittenbergae, quam à D. Bajero Anno 1676. Jenae, edito, ab utroque etiam laudato, quin novissimè à Wittenbergensi Theologo, D. Hannekenio, exasciato dicto, Declarat. Theol. de vera August. Conf. Estimatione Quaest. Prelim. 4. sub finem. pag. 6. cujus Judicii Chemniziani verba ita habent:

lemmas.gloss: not to be attacked or rejected

lemmas.note: Hannekenius polish of the Chemnitz dictum

choices.why: exascio = plane with an adze; Hannekenius polished the dictum
